subject: Every Other Week Trash Transition
overview: The council discussed Medford's shift toward every-other-week trash collection and the expansion of the city's composting program. Members reviewed strategies for community education on waste reduction and scheduled upcoming outreach events.

items.title: Approval of Minutes and Next Meeting Date
items.summary: The council approved the minutes from the previous meeting and scheduled the next meeting for February 18.

items.title: Waste Management and Composting Policy Update
items.summary: Director of Planning, Development, and Sustainability Alicia Hunt explained the history of Medford's trash contracts and the plan to transition to every-other-week trash pickup by 2027 to incentivize composting. The discussion addressed the 'pay-as-you-throw' state grant and the need for improved public messaging regarding waste disposal limits.

items.title: Waste Reduction Strategies and Demographic Outreach
items.summary: Council members discussed addressing waste management pain points for large families, seniors, and non-English speaking communities. The group explored specific waste reduction tactics, including cloth diapering support networks and the use of latching bins for dog waste to manage odors and pests.

items.title: Communication Methods for Renters and Residents
items.summary: The committee discussed the difficulties of reaching renters with physical mailers and proposed using digital channels, student-led video projects, and welcome packets for new residents. Plans were made to coordinate with Medford Community Media to broadcast educational segments on electricity and waste.

items.title: Review of Upcoming Community Events
items.summary: The council reviewed upcoming dates for Black History Month celebrations, Lunar New Year, Haitian Flag Day, and several National Grid and ABCD utility bill checkup events. Members discussed integrating interactive environmental games into multicultural night activities to engage children in recycling education.

items.title: Sustainability and Open Space Updates
items.summary: Staff provided updates on the Electrify Medford program, the launch of pollinator gardens under the 'Adopt-a-Site' program, and upcoming free tree distributions for specific neighborhoods. The group also briefly discussed environmental concerns regarding PFAS chemicals in artificial turf and the maintenance challenges of natural grass fields.
